examples.ko: 이 차선은 시간대에 따라 가변으로 운영돼요.
examples.en: This lane is operated flexibly depending on the time of day.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 높이가 가변이라서 키에 맞춰 조절해요.
examples.en: The height of this chair is adjustable, so you set it to your height.

examples.ko: 가변 좌석이 있어서 공간을 넓게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: There are adjustable seats, so you can use the space widely.
The schedule is subject to change, so I'll let you know once it's fixed.

examples.ko: 요금이 가변적으로 바뀌어서 미리 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: The fare changes depending on conditions, so you should check beforehand.
This rule can vary depending on the situation.

explain: 반대말은 '고정'이고, '가변 좌석', '가변 차선'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 일정이나 상황처럼 바뀔 수 있는 것에는 '가변적'이라고도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '바뀔 수 있는'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 극장의 가변 좌석은 공연에 따라 바꿀 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The theater's flexible seating can be changed depending on the show.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가변'을 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 대표적인 예예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical example of attaching 가변 before a noun.

phrases.en: The schedule can change, so it isn't certain yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가변'보다 서술어로 쓰기 쉬운 형태로, 바뀔 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier predicate form meaning 'subject to change'.

phrases.en: A reversible lane operates during rush hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간에 따라 방향이나 쓰임이 바뀌는 도로 차선이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A road lane whose direction or use changes with the time of day.

explain_en: Its opposite is '고정' (fixed), and it is often placed before a noun as in '가변 좌석' or '가변 차선'. For things that may change, like schedules or situations, '가변적' is also used. In casual talk people often say '바뀔 수 있는' instead.

examples.en: People's outfits in the park are all different.
Balloons of every color floated up into the sky.
The students' dreams are all different, which is interesting.
All sorts of reactions came out.
The umbrellas opened in every color.
In autumn, the mountain's leaves are of every color.

explain: 색깔뿐 아니라 모양, 생각, 반응이 각각 다를 때도 써요. '가지가지'는 종류가 많은 걸, '가지각색'은 서로 다르게 다양한 걸 강조해요. '가지각색이다', '가지각색의'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The colors of the flowers are really varied.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 '서로 다 다르다'는 뜻으로 문장을 끝낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 이다, it ends a sentence to say that things are all different.

phrases.en: There are all sorts of clothes at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 의, it modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The shop has all kinds of fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가지각색'은 서로 다른 것을, '가지가지'는 종류가 많다는 것을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 가지각색 stresses that they differ; 가지가지 stresses that there are many kinds.

explain_en: It covers not only colors but also shapes, opinions and reactions that all differ. '가지가지' stresses many kinds, while '가지각색' stresses that each is different. It is typically said as '가지각색이다' or '가지각색의'.

en: to be strange; to be weird; to be odd

examples.en: I heard a weird sound in the forest and got scared.

examples.ko: 그 건물은 모양이 괴이해서 눈길을 끌어요.
examples.en: That building catches the eye because its shape is so odd.

examples.ko: 괴이하게도 그날 밤 시계가 모두 멈췄어요.
examples.en: Strangely enough, all the clocks stopped that night.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 행동이 너무 괴이해서 다들 피했어요.
examples.en: His behavior was so strange that everyone avoided him.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 분위기가 괴이하지만 자꾸 보게 돼요.
examples.en: The mood of this painting is eerie, but I keep looking at it.

examples.ko: 오래된 집에서 괴이한 일이 계속 생겼대요.
examples.en: I heard strange things kept happening in the old house.

explain: '이상하다'보다 섬뜩하고 기이한 느낌이 있고, 말보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. '괴이하게도'처럼 문장 앞에서 놀라운 일을 소개할 때도 써요. 평소 대화에서는 '이상하다'나 '수상하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Strange things kept happening in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명하기 어려운 섬뜩한 사건을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for creepy events that are hard to explain.

phrases.example: 괴이하게도 아무도 그 방에 들어가지 못했어요.
phrases.en: Strangely enough, no one could enter that room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 앞에서 놀라운 사실을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed at the start of a sentence to introduce a surprising fact.

phrases.en: The forest at night looks eerie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 기이하고 섬뜩하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the appearance looks weird and creepy.

explain_en: It has a creepier, more uncanny feel than '이상하다' and shows up more in writing and stories than in speech. It can also open a sentence, as in '괴이하게도', to introduce something surprising. In normal conversation '이상하다' or '수상하다' sounds more natural.

en: to be sticky; to be glutinous

examples.en: In summer, my body feels sticky from sweat.
I spilled juice, so the floor is sticky.
The taffy melted and my hands started getting sticky.
Please don't touch the books with sticky hands.

examples.ko: 꿀 때문에 손가락이 끈적여서 물로 씻었어요.
examples.en: My fingers were sticky from honey, so I washed them with water.

examples.ko: 끈적일 만큼 습한 날엔 샤워를 자주 해요.
examples.en: On days humid enough to feel sticky, I shower often.

explain: 손, 바닥, 피부 같은 것이 끈끈하게 달라붙는 느낌에 써요. '끈적거리다', '끈적끈적하다'도 같은 느낌으로 말해요. 덥고 습한 날씨의 불쾌한 느낌에도 어울려요.

phrases.en: It's hot, so my whole body feels sticky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끈적이다'와 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the same meaning as '끈적이다'.

phrases.en: I got honey on my hand and it's sticky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈적한 상태가 계속될 때 더 분명하게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a clearer sense of a lasting sticky state.

phrases.en: I have to wipe the sticky floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끈적이는'은 명사 앞에서 상태를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '끈적이는' modifies a noun to show its state.

explain_en: It describes things like hands, floors or skin that feel tacky and cling. '끈적거리다' and '끈적끈적하다' give the same feeling. It also suits the unpleasant feel of hot, humid weather.

examples.en: The blue wave pattern on this curtain is pretty.
I bought a dress with a wave pattern.
I drew a wave pattern around the edge of the plate.
The wind left a wave-like pattern in the sand.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 물결무늬라서 소스가 잘 묻어요.
examples.en: This snack has a wavy pattern, so the sauce sticks well.
This cup has a handle decorated with a wave pattern.

explain: '줄무늬', '체크무늬', '물방울무늬'처럼 무늬 이름을 말할 때 써요. 물결처럼 구불구불 이어지는 모양이면 물이 아닌 모래나 천에도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I put wavy-pattern wallpaper in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽지나 천 같은 물건 앞에 붙여서 무늬를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before an item like wallpaper or fabric to describe its pattern.

phrases.en: This cup has a wave pattern.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건에 무늬가 있다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that an item has the pattern on it.

phrases.en: He came wearing a wave-pattern shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷의 무늬를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe the pattern on clothes.

explain_en: Like '줄무늬' (stripes), '체크무늬' (checks) and '물방울무늬' (polka dots), it is a pattern name. Anything that curves in a wavy line can be described this way, even sand or fabric.

examples.en: The color of the lake water is clear and blue.
In a light blue dress, you look cool and fresh.
In the sunset, the color of the water turned red.
The child gazed at the color of the water for a long time.
I painted the wall light blue.
There wasn't a single cloud in the light blue sky.

explain: 물의 색이나 연한 푸른색을 말해요. 글이나 시에서 느낌 있게 쓰이고, 일상에서는 '하늘색'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The sky-blue T-shirt looks good on you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '물빛'과 비슷한 색을 말할 때 더 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily talk for a color similar to 물빛.

phrases.example: 맑은 물빛이 너무 예뻐서 사진을 찍었어요.
phrases.en: The clear water color was so pretty that I took a picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗한 물의 색을 느낌 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the color of clean water with feeling.

phrases.en: A light-blue sky spread out in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연한 푸른색 하늘을 시적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A poetic way to describe a pale blue sky.

explain_en: It means the color of water, or a pale blue. It has a poetic feel in writing, and in daily talk people also say '하늘색'.

examples.en: I changed the poster's background color to white.

examples.ko: 바탕색이 어두워서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The background color is dark, so the text is hard to see.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 바탕색도 마음대로 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this app, you can even pick the background color freely.

examples.ko: 연한 바탕색에 진한 글씨를 쓰면 읽기 편해요.
examples.en: Dark text on a light background is easy to read.
The base color is yellow and the pattern is blue.
If the background and text colors are similar, it hurts your eyes.

explain: 그림, 천, 화면에서 맨 밑에 깔린 색을 말해요. 화면 이야기에서는 '배경색'이라고도 해요. 위에 올라오는 '글자색'이나 '무늬 색'과 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: I changed the screen background color to black.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화면이나 디자인 이야기에서 '바탕색' 대신 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used instead of 바탕색 when talking about screens or design.

phrases.en: I couldn't see the text, so I changed the base color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맨 밑에 깔린 색을 다른 색으로 고친다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means changing the bottom layer's color to another.

phrases.en: The base color and the text color are too similar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위에 올라오는 글자색과 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing with the text color on top.

explain_en: It means the underlying color in a picture, fabric or screen. For screens, people also say '배경색'. It is often mentioned together with the color on top, like '글자색' (text color) or pattern color.

en: to be reddish; to be bright-red

examples.en: My cheeks are frozen red from the cold.
The sunset has turned the sky red.
Bright red apples are hanging on the tree.
Your face is red from the sun.
Your eyes were red, so I asked if you had been crying.
The baby's cheeks are rosy and cute.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 작고 은은한 붉은색에 어울리고, 큰 것이나 짙은 느낌은 '벌겋다'와 짝을 이뤄요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 '발개요, 발간, 발갛게'처럼 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: The baby's rosy cheeks are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발갛다'가 명사를 꾸밀 때는 'ㅎ'이 빠져요.
phrases.nuance_en: When modifying a noun, the ㅎ drops out.

phrases.en: My face turned red from embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 발간 색이 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means gradually becoming red.

phrases.en: This apple isn't red yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이고, 'ㅎ'은 그대로 남아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form; the ㅎ stays.

explain_en: It suits a small or soft shade of red, more delicate than '빨갛다'. Its larger counterpart is '벌겋다'. It is an irregular ㅎ adjective, so it changes like 발개요, 발간, 발갛게.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 변칙 영업으로 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: This shop got into trouble for its irregular business practices.
The exam questions came up in an unusual way, so I was flustered.

examples.ko: 규칙에는 변칙이 있어서 따로 외워야 해요.
examples.en: The rule has exceptions, so you have to memorize them separately.
If you change the schedule in an irregular way, everyone gets inconvenienced.

examples.ko: 한국어 동사에는 변칙 활용이 많아서 어려워요.
examples.en: Korean verbs have many irregular conjugations, so they are hard.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 변칙 작전을 써서 경기를 이겼어요.
examples.en: That team won the game by using an unconventional strategy.

explain: '원칙'과 반대로 정해진 규칙에서 벗어난 방식을 말해요. 문법에서는 보통 '불규칙'이라고 하고, 운영이나 거래 이야기에서는 편법 같은 부정적인 느낌으로 '변칙 운영'처럼 써요. '변칙적으로'처럼 '-적'을 붙인 형태도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That team used an unconventional strategy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙에서 벗어난 방식을 설명할 때 쓰고, 꼭 나쁜 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a method that departs from the rules, not always negatively.

phrases.example: 버스 회사가 변칙 운영을 해서 승객이 불편했어요.
phrases.en: The bus company ran irregular service, which inconvenienced passengers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 방식과 다르게 운영한다는 부정적인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a negative sense of running things differently from the set way.

phrases.en: They handled the matter by irregular means, not by the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '원칙'과 같이 써서 차이를 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with its opposite 'wonchik' to show the contrast.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '원칙' (principle) and refers to a way that departs from the set rules. In grammar people usually say '불규칙', while in talk about operations or deals it carries a negative, workaround feel, as in '변칙 운영'. The '-적' form '변칙적으로' is also common.

examples.en: I chose a chick-yellow color for the baby's clothes.
A chick-yellow dress suits spring well.

examples.ko: 이 벽지는 병아리색이라서 방이 밝아 보여요.
examples.en: This wallpaper is chick-yellow, so the room looks bright.

examples.ko: 병아리색 말고 좀 더 진한 노란색은 없나요?
examples.en: Do you have a deeper yellow instead of chick-yellow?

examples.ko: 병아리색이 귀엽긴 한데 때가 잘 타요.
examples.en: Chick-yellow is cute, but it gets dirty easily.
My daughter likes chick-yellow the most.

explain: '노란색'보다 연하고 부드러운 느낌의 노랑을 말할 때 써요. 옷이나 아기 물건, 벽지의 색을 이야기할 때 나올 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 동생이 병아리색 옷을 입으니 정말 귀여워요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling looks so cute in the chick-yellow clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연한 노랑 옷을 말할 때 자주 써요. 아기 옷에 특히 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for light yellow clothes, especially baby clothes.

phrases.en: We painted the child's room walls chick-yellow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽이나 가구의 색을 정할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing the color of walls or furniture.

phrases.en: Light yellow is my favorite color.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병아리색'을 일반적인 말로 풀어서 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain description of what 병아리색 means.

explain_en: It is used for a yellow that is lighter and softer than plain '노란색'. It can come up when talking about the color of clothes, baby items or wallpaper.

en: to be soft; to be smooth

examples.en: The baby's skin is really soft.
This towel is soft and warm.
I slept under a soft blanket.
After I put on lotion, my hands became smooth.
The puppy's fur felt soft.

examples.ko: 보드랍지 않은 천은 아기에게 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Fabric that isn't soft is not good for babies.

explain: '부드럽다'와 비슷한데, 아기 피부나 털, 천처럼 여리고 고운 느낌에 잘 어울려요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '보드라워요', '보드라운'으로 바뀌어요. 반대말은 '거칠다'예요.

phrases.en: I held the baby's soft hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때는 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '보드라운'이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes 보드라운 because of the ㅂ irregular.

phrases.en: This fabric isn't very soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형은 규칙대로 '보드랍지 않아요'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative follows the regular pattern: 보드랍지 않아요.

phrases.en: This bread is really soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 넓게 쓰는 말이에요. 음식, 목소리, 성격에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also works for food, voices, and personalities.

explain_en: It is close to '부드럽다', but fits a delicate, fine feel such as a baby's skin, fur or fabric. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '보드라워요' and '보드라운'. The opposite is '거칠다' (rough).

en: to be strict; to be precise

examples.ko: 엄밀하게 말하면 이 두 단어는 뜻이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Strictly speaking, these two words have slightly different meanings.
The experiment must be carried out under precise conditions.
If you look at it strictly, it isn't my fault.

examples.ko: 보고서의 숫자를 엄밀하게 확인한 뒤에 제출했어요.
examples.en: I submitted the report after checking the numbers carefully.

examples.ko: 그 교수님은 자료를 엄밀하게 검토하기로 유명해요.
examples.en: That professor is known for reviewing data with great rigor.
In the strict sense, a whale is not a fish.

explain: '엄밀히 말하면', '엄밀한 의미에서'처럼 말할 때 가장 많이 나와요. '엄격하다'는 규칙이나 태도가 빡빡하다는 뜻이고, '엄밀하다'는 빈틈없이 정확하게 따진다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Strictly speaking, this isn't a lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확하게 따져서 말할 때 문장 앞에 붙이는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common opener when you want to speak with strict accuracy.

phrases.example: 엄밀하게 따지면 제 잘못이 더 커요.
phrases.en: If you look at it strictly, my fault is greater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빈틈없이 자세히 따져 볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for examining something carefully and without gaps.

phrases.example: 엄밀한 의미에서 그 일은 취미가 아니에요.
phrases.en: In the strict sense, that is not a hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어의 정확한 뜻을 기준으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking by the exact meaning of a word.

explain_en: It most often appears in phrases like '엄밀히 말하면' and '엄밀한 의미에서'. '엄격하다' is about strict rules or attitudes, while '엄밀하다' is about examining something precisely with no gaps.

examples.en: When spring comes, the mountains take on a light yellow-green color.
The fields in early spring are completely light green.
Light green sprouts have come up out of the ground.
The willow leaves sparkle yellow-green in the sunlight.
Wearing a light green dress makes it feel like spring.
Light yellow-green is a color that rests the eyes.

explain: 초록보다 밝고 노란 기운이 도는 봄 새잎의 색이에요. '연두색'과 거의 같게 쓰는데, '-빛'은 색이 비치는 느낌을 더해서 자연이나 풍경을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Wearing a yellowish-green outfit feels like spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 물건의 색을 말할 때는 '연두색'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the color of clothes or objects, 연두색 is more common.

phrases.en: Yellowish-green leaves came out on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄에 새로 나온 잎을 예쁘게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when describing new leaves in spring.

phrases.en: When spring came, the mountain turned yellowish green.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경의 색이 서서히 바뀌는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes scenery gradually changing color.

explain_en: It is the bright, slightly yellowish green of new spring leaves. It is used almost like '연두색', but '-빛' adds a sense of color glowing or showing through, so it suits nature and scenery.

en: to be dusky; to be dingy; to be dark

examples.ko: 벽 색이 너무 칙칙해서 방이 어두워 보여요.
examples.en: The wall color is so dull that the room looks dark.

examples.ko: 칙칙한 얼굴색에는 밝은 립스틱이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: A bright lipstick suits a dull complexion well.
Most winter clothes are drab.

examples.ko: 그 옷은 색이 칙칙하지 않아서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like that outfit because the color isn't dull.
The dingy alley became bright thanks to the murals.
When you're tired, your skin looks dull.

explain: 색이나 분위기가 밝지 않고 탁할 때 써요. 옷, 벽, 피부, 골목에 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 반대는 '화사하다'나 '산뜻하다'예요.

phrases.example: 칙칙한 색 옷은 얼굴이 어두워 보여요.
phrases.en: Dull-colored clothes make your face look dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밝지 않고 탁한 색을 말할 때 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, for colors that are not bright and look muddy.

phrases.example: 벽 색 때문에 방이 칙칙해 보여요.
phrases.en: The room looks dingy because of the wall color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 분위기가 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks or feels dingy.

phrases.en: You look bright in light-colored clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칙칙하다'의 반대말이에요. 밝고 환한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 칙칙하다: bright and radiant.

explain_en: It is used when a color or mood is not bright and looks murky. It works for clothes, walls, skin, and alleys. The opposites are '화사하다' and '산뜻하다'.

en: to be special; to be particular; to be specialized

examples.en: This job requires a special skill.
The situation is a bit unusual.
It is allowed only in special cases.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 특수하게 만든 옷을 팔아요.
examples.en: That company sells specially made clothes.
The environment was unusual, so it was hard to adapt.

examples.ko: 이곳은 특수했던 시대의 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This place holds a story from a special era.

explain: '특수하다'는 보통과 달라서 한정된 경우나 목적에 맞다는 느낌이에요. '특별하다'는 좋은 의미로 소중하거나 뛰어나다고 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '특수 효과', '특수 상황'처럼 붙여서도 써요.

phrases.en: In special cases, please tell me first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보통과 다른 한정된 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for limited situations that differ from the usual.

phrases.en: This problem is not that special.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보통과 다르지 않다고 부정할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not unusual.

phrases.example: 이 영화는 특수 효과가 정말 좋아요.
phrases.en: This movie has really good special effects.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특수'를 앞에 붙여 한 낱말처럼 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase where '특수' is attached in front like one word.

explain_en: 특수하다 carries the feel of being different from the usual and fitted to a limited case or purpose. 특별하다 is used more when saying something is precious or outstanding in a good way. It also attaches to nouns, as in 특수 효과 (special effects) and 특수 상황 (special situation).

en: blue or green hue; bluish tint

examples.en: The sea sparkles blue in the early morning.
That bottle gives off a soft bluish glow.
A bluish tint began to appear in the dawn sky.

examples.ko: 푸른빛 원피스가 너한테 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The blue dress really suits you.
At the forest lake, all you can see is blue-green.
Just looking at blue makes my mind feel refreshed.

explain: '푸르다'는 하늘이나 바다 같은 파란색뿐 아니라 풀과 나무의 초록색에도 써요. 그래서 '푸른빛'도 파란 느낌인지 초록 느낌인지는 대상을 보고 알 수 있어요. '푸른빛이 돌다', '푸른빛을 띠다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: There is a bluish tint in the dawn sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 약하게 보일 때 '돌다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 돌다 when the color shows faintly.

phrases.en: This glass has a blue tint.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 색을 가지고 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something as having a certain color.
phrases.en_equiv: to take on a blue hue

phrases.en: The night sea sparkles in blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 나는 모습을 말할 때 '으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '으로' to describe something shining in that color.

explain_en: '푸르다' covers not only the blue of sky and sea but also the green of grass and trees. So '푸른빛' may feel blue or green depending on what it describes. It often appears as '푸른빛이 돌다' or '푸른빛을 띠다'.

examples.ko: 서울과 지방의 집값이 지금도 현격히 달라요.
examples.en: Housing prices in Seoul and the provinces are still markedly different.

examples.ko: 작년보다 우리 가게 매출이 현격히 줄었어요.
examples.en: Our shop's sales have dropped considerably compared with last year.

examples.ko: 새 약을 먹은 뒤로 증상이 현격히 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Since I started the new medicine, my symptoms have improved significantly.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 실력 차이가 현격히 커서 경기가 싱거웠어요.
examples.en: The skill gap between the two teams was so big that the match was dull.
My memory has declined markedly as I've gotten older.
Has this exam become significantly easier than the last one?

explain: '차이, 줄다, 늘다, 달라지다'처럼 변화나 차이를 나타내는 말과 자주 같이 써요. '많이'나 '크게'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스, 보고서, 발표에서 더 자주 들려요. 비슷한 말로 '확연히'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 두 지역 사이에 현격한 차이가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a marked difference between the two regions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '현격히'의 형용사형으로, 차이가 아주 크다는 점을 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, stating formally that a gap is very large.

phrases.en: The number of tourists has increased markedly this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자나 양이 눈에 띄게 많아졌다고 보고하듯이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report in a report-like tone that a number or amount clearly grew.

phrases.en: It has changed clearly from before.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현격히보다 부드럽고, 눈에 뚜렷이 보인다는 느낌이 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 현격히, with the sense that something is clearly visible.

explain_en: It pairs often with words of change or difference such as 차이 (gap), 줄다 (decrease), 늘다 (increase) and 달라지다 (change). It sounds more formal than '많이' or '크게', so you hear it more in news, reports and presentations. A similar word is '확연히'.
